elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: 14.1 as rendered retains: "RevMed shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Sanofi, its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, agents and employees ('Sanofi Indemnitees')" — express defence duty running to Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: "from and against any Third Party Claims and Losses arising therefrom under or related to this Agreement against any of them"; "Third Party Claims" is defined at 1.126 and "Losses" at 1.60.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: New 14.1(d): "any allegation that the RevMed Licensed Technology, or the Research, Development, Manufacture or Commercialization of any SHP2 Inhibitor or Product in accordance with this Agreement, infringes or misappropriates the intellectual property rights of any Third Party". The deterministic check "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present" returned false, but that is a false negative keyed to the model wording "Services or Deliverables"; substantively the inserted limb covers third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims arising from what Vendor supplies and from exploitation of the Product.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: New 14.1(e): "RevMed's breach of Applicable Law". ("Applicable Law" is used as a defined term elsewhere in the Agreement, including in the parallel 14.2(b); confirm the capitalised definition exists so the limb is not left undefined.)

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: New 14.1(f): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Sanofi's Confidential Information or other data of Sanofi caused by RevMed".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.1(a): "the negligence, recklessness or willful misconduct of any of the RevMed Indemnitees" — ordinary negligence is broader than, and subsumes, gross negligence, and wilful misconduct is expressly named.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: 14.3(a) Notice of Claim: "The Indemnified Party will give the indemnifying Party ... prompt written notice (an 'Indemnification Claim Notice') of any Losses ...", retained unchanged.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: 14.3(b) Control of Defense: "At its option, the Indemnifying Party may assume the defense of any Third Party Claim subject to indemnification as provided for in Section 14.1 or Section 14.2 ...", retained unchanged and now automatically extends to the new 14.1 limbs.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: 14.3(e) Cooperation: "the Indemnified Party will, and will cause each other Indemnitee to, cooperate in the defense thereof and will furnish such records, information and testimony ... as may be reasonably requested".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: 14.2 as rendered reads only: "(a) content, data or materials provided by Sanofi to RevMed; or (b) Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law; or (c) [Intentionally omitted]; or (d) [Intentionally omitted]" — the former Research/Development/Manufacture/Commercialization limb and the breach-of-warranty and breach-of-obligation limbs are struck.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: New 14.1(d) covers Third Party Claims alleging infringement or misappropriation of Third Party intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no Customer-modification carve-out is added, which is more favourable to Customer; the retained exceptions ((i) Sanofi negligence/recklessness/wilful misconduct, (ii) Sanofi breach of warranties, (iii) Sanofi breach of obligations) do not require one.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination carve-out is present and none is required. Absence favours Customer.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no Customer-specification carve-out is present and none is required.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: No procure/modify/replace remedy appears anywhere in the rendered 14.1–14.3 language; only defence and indemnification are provided.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees fallback remedy is drafted; the clause contains no monetary refund mechanic tied to unavailable IP remedies.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual fees super-cap (or any cap) is stated in the rendered indemnity language.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all ten preferred elements are met on the operative text. The pre-existing 14.1 chapeau already supplies the defend/indemnify/hold-harmless duty to Sanofi and its Affiliates against Third Party Claims, 14.1(a) supplies negligence/wilful misconduct, and 14.3(a), (b) and (e) supply notice, control of defence and cooperation; the three inserted limbs (d) IP infringement, (e) breach of Applicable Law and (f) Vendor-caused unauthorised access/disclosure close the identified gaps.

The deterministic signal "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present: false" is a false negative: it appears keyed to the model phrase "Services or Deliverables infringe", whereas the inserted 14.1(d) covers infringement/misappropriation of Third Party intellectual property arising from the RevMed Licensed Technology and from Research/Development/Manufacture/Commercialization of the SHP2 Inhibitor or Product. In substance the IP indemnity exists.

Fallback is not complete (no procure/modify/replace, no refund, no 3x super-cap), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is fully met; the rationale correctly explains that the super-cap would in fact worsen a currently uncapped indemnity.

Minimality holds: the only edits are the three new Vendor limbs required by preferred elements 3–5, the conforming update of the exception chapeau from the old lettering to "((a) through (f))", and the narrowing of 14.2 to the two categories the checklist permits. No survival tail, expense language, extra damages categories or boilerplate has been added, and the notice/control/cooperation machinery is untouched.

Intent is preserved: the Sanofi-fault carve-outs in 14.1 ((i)-(iii)) are retained and now correctly extend across the new limbs, so allocation between the parties is coherent, and 14.3's procedure applies to the amended 14.1 and 14.2 without contradiction.

Drafting point to verify before sending: the rendered 14.1 runs (a), (c), (d)-(f) with no (b) shown and no "[Intentionally omitted]" placeholder, while the exception chapeau still reads "in each case ((a) through (f))". Confirm that the original 14.1(b) (RevMed's material breach of its warranties/representations) is retained in full — silently dropping that Customer-favourable limb would be both a minimality and an intent failure, and leaving the range reference over a deleted sub-clause would create a dangling cross-reference. If (b) was intentionally removed, restore it; if retained, show it in the redline.
Also confirm that "Applicable Law" is a capitalised defined term in the Agreement so that new 14.1(e) and 14.2(b) do not introduce an undefined term.

Finding status "deviation" is correct: the unamended 14.1 had no IP-infringement, breach-of-law or data-breach cover while Article XIII disclaims non-infringement, and 14.2 imposed a far broader Customer indemnity than the playbook permits.
